_README: The single source of truth for the native side of the mod API.
and the telemetry audit. Change it here and everything follows.
1. Find it by symbol name in the Android client's libtriarch.so (ARM64) for the signature.
2. Find its x86 twin structurally - never assume an offset transfers.
3. Read its terminating `ret` immediate. Every ret in one function shares
the same immediate; if they disagree you are looking at TWO functions
packed without int3 padding (this is what OpenCharacterMenu does).
4. Add an entry. The resolver asserts sum(stack widths) == ret imm and
REFUSES to emit the entry otherwise. No rebuild of the stub is needed.
i32 u32 vid vnum f32 ptr cstr bool32 = 4    i64 u64 f64 = 8
`this` travels in ECX and is NOT part of the stack total.
TRUST: this is a TRUSTED-MOD API, not a sandbox. `capability`, `safety`,
`side_effects` and `requires` are recorded but NOT yet enforced - they exist
so enforcement can be switched on later without re-migrating every entry.

natives.name: FindAndSetNewTarget

args.name: main
args.doc: the player's own CInstanceBase, from api.player.main_instance

natives.doc: Whole acquisition in one call: FindVictim (including the 100-sample line-of-sight ray march that is unreachable from Python), targeting, __OnPressActor and the walk-in. Measured 50 acquisitions, 0 faults.

natives.name: OnPressActor
natives.doc: Set the auto-attack target. Sets the VID and the cached actor pointer together, which is what keeps them consistent - hand-writing those fields instead is what would trip __key__b0t__ on builds that have it.

natives.name: UseAutoSkills

args.name: target
args.doc: may be NULL - buffs do not need a target

natives.doc: Buffs, attack skills, cooldowns, mana and range, from the skill list picked in the autohunt window. NOTE `now` is 64-bit: it occupies two stack slots, which is why stack_bytes is 16 for three arguments. EMITS: SendUseSkillPacket normally, and /user_horse_ride if the character is MOUNTED - hence the not-mounted precondition.

natives.name: OpenCharacterMenu
natives.doc: Called by AutoHuntLoop right after __OnPressActor. Its region holds TWO functions with no int3 between them - the trailing `ret 0xc` belongs to the next one, this is `ret 4`.

natives.name: UpdateAutoAttack
natives.doc: One frame of the attack sustain. The client already calls this every frame from CPythonPlayer::Update; exposed for diagnostics, not for driving.

natives.name: CreateAutoBotSettings
natives.doc: Rebuilds the autohunt settings block from CPythonConfig (hunt_use_skill, hunt_use_mount, hunt_type, hunt_items, hunt_support). Audited over its true bounds (2813 bytes): zero SendChatPacket calls, no network/minimap/player singleton reference. Also reachable as playerm2g2.CreateAutoBotSettings.

natives.name: SendChatPacket
natives.doc: DELIBERATELY UNPLACED (area null) so it is not reachable as api.<area>.SendChatPacket. Anything sending /auto_hunt would put this client into the developers' live autohunt analytics - the one thing the isolation rule forbids. Reach it explicitly if you must.

rejected.name: FindVictim
rejected.detail: Takes its float `range` argument in XMM2, not on the stack: its first instruction is `movss [esp+0x20], xmm2`, and the caller does `movaps xmm2, xmm0` before the call. Stack cleanup is ret 0x10 = 4 dwords, so the float is genuinely enregistered and the declared signature would be wrong in a way that corrupts the stack rather than raising. The trampoline supports stack arguments only, so this FAILS CLOSED.
rejected.use_instead: FindAndSetNewTarget - it calls FindVictim, computes the search radius from the minimap slider itself ((value + 40) * 35), applies the line-of-sight filter and engages.
rejected.to_support_later: Add an explicit ABI variant (e.g. x86-msvc-thiscall-xmm2f) that the trampoline honours by loading declared float arguments into XMM registers. Opt-in per entry, never inferred.

fields.name: auto_attack_vid
fields.doc: The current auto-attack target VID, 0 when unengaged. READ ONLY on purpose: it must stay consistent with the cached actor pointer 4 bytes above it. Use OnPressActor to set, DropEngagement to clear.

fields.name: auto_attack_target
fields.doc: The CACHED ACTOR POINTER that sits 4 bytes above the auto-attack VID. UseAutoSkills takes it as pTarget. Read-only: it must stay consistent with the VID beside it, which is what __OnPressActor guarantees and a hand-write would not.

fields.name: hunt_use_skill
fields.doc: The autohunt window's 'use skills' checkbox. UseAutoSkills tests this first and returns immediately when clear.

fields.name: hunt_use_mount
fields.doc: The autohunt window's 'use mount' checkbox, the byte just above hunt_use_skill. UseAutoSkills dismounts to cast an attack skill and only REMOUNTS afterwards when this is set; clear, and it stays dismounted. Set it to drive the client's own dismount->cast->remount cycle.

fields.name: hunt_stones
fields.doc: The 'stones only' choice. AutoHuntLoop reads this byte at both of its FindAndSetNewTarget call sites.

fields.name: player_state
fields.doc: Player state enum; 0x89 is the charge-skill state __OnPressActor tests for.

fields.name: hunt_anchor
fields.doc: The point FindVictim searches around - NOT the character position. Two floats.

fields.name: hunt_skills
fields.doc: The configured skill slots. A std::vector<BYTE> begin/end POINTER PAIR, not a value - exposed through an adapter that returns a list. Raw access to this offset is meaningless and is not offered.

fields.name: auto_move_active
fields.doc: True while a walk-to-waypoint is in progress. Set by CPythonPlayer::AutoMoveToPosition once the route is accepted; cleared on arrival, on cancel, and when no path can be built. Covers BOTH a mod calling api.move_to and the player clicking the atlas, because every route goes through that one function.

fields.name: auto_move_enabled
fields.doc: Set alongside auto_move_active when a route is accepted. Reading BOTH tells a stuck 'active' apart from a genuinely live route.

fields.name: auto_move_dest
fields.doc: Destination (x, y) the current route is heading to, written by CPythonPlayer::AutoMoveToPosition just before the active flag. Diagnostic: a stale destination with active=1 means the flag was never cleared.

instance_fields.name: mounted
instance_fields.doc: IsMountingHorse(), which this build inlines as a byte on CInstanceBase. Every /user_horse_ride UseAutoSkills can emit is downstream of it, which is why 'not mounted' is a provable guarantee of silence rather than a heuristic.
